responses.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent) AS avg_amount_minus_spent, COUNT(*) AS num_budget_lines FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.spent > 6.0 GROUP BY e.status

assumptions.assumption: AVG ignores NULLs in amount - spent, so it returns NULL (blank) when no values exist; the count includes all qualifying budget lines (spent > 6.0 implies spent is non-null), regardless of whether amount is null.

responses.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent) AS avg_amount_minus_spent, COUNT(*) AS num_budget_lines FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.spent > 6.0 GROUP BY e.status

assumptions.assumption: The status is event.status (the status of the linked event), not budget.event_status. Grouping is by event.status.

The average is AVG(amount - spent) per row. Rows with a NULL amount or spent are skipped, so the average is NULL if none remain. The count covers all qualifying budget lines, including any with NULL amount.

responses.sql: SELECT e.status AS status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent) AS avg_amount_minus_spent, COUNT(*) AS line_count FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.spent > 6.0 GROUP BY e.status

assumptions.assumption: AVG ignores NULLs, which yields NULL (blank) when no non-null values exist; the count is the number of qualifying budget lines (COUNT(*)) per event status, including lines whose amount is NULL.
